dialogue.content:
# Plan: camera intensity stability over ~60 s

## Quantity and definition
The quantity is the spatially averaged dark-corrected intensity of a fixed ROI, I(t) in DN, for each frame over about 60 s. Drift is the systematic change of I(t) over the minute. Frame-to-frame noise is treated separately.

## Physics and formulas
- Per frame: I_k = mean(ROI pixels) − D, where D is the mean dark level from the dark frames.
- Temporal noise of the ROI mean is small (about sqrt(var_pixel/N_pix)), so the drift is detectable when it exceeds this level.
- Linear drift: fit I_k = a + b·t_k. Report b in DN/s, drift per minute = 60·b, and relative drift = 60·b / mean(I) in %/min.
- Endpoint change: (mean of last 10 frames − mean of first 10 frames) / mean of first 10 frames.
- Peak-to-peak range: (max − min) / mean of the smoothed series.
- Fluctuation: std(I)/mean(I) after removing the linear trend. Drift is significant if |b| is larger than 3 times its standard error from the fit.
- Exposure choice: the brightest ROI pixels should reach about 50–70% of full scale, with no pixel at the saturation level (255 for 8-bit, 1023 for 10-bit, 4095 for 12-bit; use the pixel format actually set). Stay below saturation so that clipping cannot mask drift.

## Settings
- Fixed exposure, fixed gain (lowest gain), and auto-exposure, auto-gain and auto-white-balance all off. Pixel format Mono, 12-bit if available, otherwise 8-bit.
- Exposure: set by a short test so that the ROI peak is at 50–70% of full scale. Record the value used. It must stay within the camera's range and the lab limits.
- Frame rate: fixed at about 5 fps through the frame-rate enable setting, or by software timing. Check the exposure time is shorter than the frame period.
- Frames: about 300 over about 60 s. This does not have to be exact, but the actual timestamps must be recorded.
- The light source should be on and warmed up for the usual lab time before the run. Do not touch the setup during the run.

## Numbered steps
1. [hardware] Connect to the camera. Disable auto-exposure, auto-gain and auto-white-balance, set gain to minimum, set the pixel format, and read back and record all settings, including the sensor temperature if the camera exposes it.
2. [hardware] Take a short test capture of a few frames with the light on. Check the maximum pixel value and adjust the exposure until the brightest pixel is at 50–70% of full scale. Then fix the exposure.
3. [hardware] Capture 20 dark frames (light blocked or source off, same exposure and gain) and save them as dark_XXX.
4. [hardware] Capture the main series: about 300 frames at about 5 fps, light on, fixed settings. Save every frame losslessly (PNG or raw/TIFF, not JPEG), with a per-frame timestamp (a timestamps file with the host time and the camera timestamp if available). Name them stab_XXXX.
5. [hardware] Capture another 20 dark frames at the end, to check whether the dark level itself drifted. Save them as dark_end_XXX.
6. [analysis] One Python script on the saved frames:
   - Load the dark frames and compute D_start and D_end (mean DN).
   - Load the stability frames and define the ROI as a central region (for example 200×200 px), or the region containing the bright area. Compute I_k, the max pixel in the ROI and the saturated pixel count for each frame.
   - Fit the linear trend and compute the noise statistics defined above.
   - Print NAME=value lines: N_FRAMES, DURATION_S, MEAN_DN, DARK_START_DN, DARK_END_DN, DARK_DRIFT_DN, MAX_PIXEL_DN, SATURATED_PIXELS, SLOPE_DN_PER_S, DRIFT_DN_PER_MIN, DRIFT_PERCENT_PER_MIN, SLOPE_SIGMA, ENDPOINT_CHANGE_PERCENT, PTP_PERCENT, STD_DETRENDED_PERCENT.
7. [analysis] Validity checks in the same script. Print SATURATION_OK (0 saturated pixels), DARK_STABLE_OK (dark drift much smaller than the light drift) and TIMING_OK (the maximum gap between frames is below 2 times the median gap). If any of them fail, report the drift as unreliable and say why.
8. Report: the drift as %/min with its uncertainty, the endpoint change, the noise level, and whether the drift is significant. Only quote numbers that the script printed.

Instruction: Execute plan steps 1-5 with the camera MCP tools. 1) Connect; auto-exposure, auto-gain and auto-white-balance off; gain minimum; Mono, 12-bit if available (else 8-bit); read back and report all settings (and sensor temperature if available). 2) Take a few test frames with the light on; tune exposure so the brightest pixel is at 50-70% of full scale with no saturation; fix it and report the value. 3) Capture 20 dark frames (light blocked, or report if you cannot block it) and save them as dark_XXX. 4) Capture the main series: about 300 frames at about 5 fps (about 60 s), fixed settings, saved losslessly as stab_XXXX, with a timestamps file (host time, plus camera time if available). If the tools limit the frame count or rate, capture as many as allowed over about 60 s and report the actual numbers. 5) Capture 20 more dark frames as dark_end_XXX. Report the file paths, directory, settings, pixel format, max pixel in the test frames and the actual frame count and duration. Do not touch the setup during the run.
